text:
Carla (Product): quick design review — can we sync on the model catalog changes? specifically: badge prioritization in the compare table, the pin UI affordance for version pinning, and filter state persistence across routes.

Anya (Design): thanks — posted updated comps in figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz. main changes: 1) compact badges (left-aligned stack), 2) pin as a context action (hover-only) + persistent pin chip in header, 3) filter state saved per workspace.

Ben (Eng): saw the comps. hover-only pin might be tricky for keyboard users. also need to think about how many badges we render before truncation — rendering 6 badges per row kills layout. maybe lazy-show extra badges behind a "+n" menu?

Dave (Accessibility): +1 on keyboard concerns. hover-only = invisible to keyboard. we should always render a focusable pin button with an aria-label like: `aria-label="Pin model version for compare"` and `aria-pressed` state. also contrast on the light badge background is low — need 4.5:1 for body text.

Anya (Design): good catch. proposal: always show a subtle pin icon (outline) that becomes filled when pinned. visible but low-visual-weight. we can hide the bulk of badges behind a collapsed list that is expandable. for keyboard, tab should land on pin and on the expand control.

Oliver (PM): UX question: if a user pins a version from the compare modal, should that pin persist when they navigate back to the catalog? current ask from enterprise customers is persistence across sessions for rollout reproducibility.

Carla (Product): customers want pinned versions to survive navigation and be part of the route (so they can share links). suggestion: include pin state in URL as a query param (e.g., `?pin=v2.3`).

Ben (Eng): including in URL is fine but watch for long lists. maybe canonical approach: `?pin=model-id@version` and store a short alias in local storage when used often. server can ignore but console reads it.

Dave (Accessibility): also recommend visible affordance for screen reader users when pin state changes: `aria-live=\"polite\"` region announcing \"Version v2.3 pinned for compare\".

Anya (Design): microcopy: current tooltip says \"Pin\" — ambiguous. alternatives: \"Pin version for future compares\" or \"Pin this version (keeps it in compare)\" — prefer the shorter one. thoughts?

Carla (Product): lean toward \"Pin version for compare\" to keep it short. product note: add secondary tooltip on hover that says \"This version will persist in your compare view and shareable link.\"

Ben (Eng): implementation nit: avoid tooltips for essential state — they should be supplemental. ensure visual state communicates pinned vs unpinned (filled icon + chip in header).

Anya (Design): agreed. also variant for mobile: replace hover interactions with a three-dot menu that surfaces pin + badges list.

Oliver (PM): routing: if pin is in URL, need to consider rollout toggles. what happens when pinned version is deprecated? fallback behavior?

Carla (Product): fallback: if a pinned version is gone, show placeholder card with CTA \"Select replacement\" and an inline note \"Pinned version is no longer available — showing closest match.\" also surface a small badge \"deprecated\" for clarity.

Ben (Eng): engineers: let's add a compatibility layer in the frontend: try exact match -> if missing, fetch metadata to find latest minor -> if none, mark as missing. fallback should not break compare table layout.

Dave (Accessibility): quick a11y checklist for the change: 1) pin button accessible by keyboard (Enter/Space) 2) aria-pressed for state 3) aria-live reminder on change 4) badge contrast >= 4.5 5) expand/collapse control has `aria-expanded`. I'll add a short spec.

Anya (Design): compact badges: new visual system: max 3 inline badges + "+n" overflow. overflow opens a popover with list view that supports keyboard arrows + typeahead. also consider showing a performance metric badge (p95 latency) only when available.

Carla (Product): on performance badges — we debated whether they should be primary signal in compare table. ops wants latency/cost visible, but designers worry about noise. proposal: show one primary performance badge (p95 latency) and hide others behind overflow. also allow users to toggle metrics columns.

Ben (Eng): toggling columns is ok but expensive to persist per-user. we can persist in local storage per workspace, and optionally in the cloud for logged-in teams later.

Oliver (PM): metrics badges should have hover state that opens a mini-trend sparkline and a timestamp of last sample. don't show exact values by default to avoid signal noise.

Anya (Design): copy for the performance badge tooltip: \"p95 latency — measured across recent production requests. Click to see the trend.\"

Dave (Accessibility): make sure sparklines have accessible descriptions — either a visually hidden text: \"p95 latency trend: 120ms → 130ms → 110ms\" or `role=\"img\" aria-label=\"p95 latency trend\"`.

Carla (Product): next steps: Anya to update comps with persistent pin chip in header, overflow + +n handling, and microcopy changes. Ben to prototype pin button markup and URL sync. Dave to publish a short a11y checklist. I'll gather customer feedback from the pilot group and circle back.

DesignBot: task created: \"Update model catalog comps — pin affordance & badges\" assigned to Anya, due 2026-04-02. :white_check_mark:

Ben (Eng): acked. will spike the URL param flow this week.

Anya (Design): will push new frames by EOD and add keyboard flows in the spec.

Carla (Product): thanks everyone. if you spot any copy/regression nits in the new frames ping me directly. :thumbsup:
